{{short description|Hierarchy that deals with part–whole relationships}}
{{Distinguish|Meronymy and holonymy{{!}}Meronymy|Metonymy}}

A '''meronomy''' is a hierarchical [[taxonomy]] that deals with part–whole relationships. For example, a car has parts that include engine, body and wheels; and the body has parts that include doors and windows. 

These conceptual structures are used in [[linguistics]] and [[computer science]], with applications in [[biology]]. The part–whole relationship is sometimes referred to as ''HAS-A'', and corresponds to object composition in [[object-oriented programming]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Object-Oriented Programming Concept |url=http://www.javacamp.org/moreclasses/oop/oop3.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403035509/http://www.javacamp.org:80/moreclasses/oop/oop3.html |archive-date=2018-04-03 |access-date=2025-05-03 |website=www.javacamp.org |language=en}}</ref> 

The study of meronomy is known as ''[[mereology]]'', and in linguistics a ''meronym'' is the name given to a constituent part of, a substance of, or a member of something. "X" is a meronym of "Y" if an X is a part of a Y.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Princeton University Cognitive Science Laboratory |url=http://wordnet.princeton.edu/gloss |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080512144133/http://wordnet.princeton.edu/gloss |archive-date=2008-05-12 |access-date=2025-05-03 |website=wordnet.princeton.edu |language=en-US}}</ref> The unit of organisation that corresponds to the taxonomical '''taxon''' is the '''meron'''.

== Example ==
*Cars have parts: engine, headlight, wheel
**Engines have parts: crankcase, carburetor
**Headlights have parts: headlight bulb, reflector
**Wheels have parts: rim, spokes, tires

== In knowledge representation ==
In formal terms, in the context of [[knowledge representation]] and [[ontologies]], a meronomy is a [[partially ordered set|partial order]] of concept types by the part–whole [[relation (mathematics)|relation]].<ref>[http://www.jfsowa.com/ontology/gloss.htm Glossary<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

In the classic study of parts and wholes, [[mereology]], the three defining properties of a partial order serve as [[axioms]].<ref>[http://www.w3.org/2001/sw/BestPractices/OEP/SimplePartWhole/ Simple part-whole relations in OWL Ontologies<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> They are, respectively, that the part-of relation is:

* [[Transitive relation|Transitive]] – "Parts of parts are parts of the whole" (If ''A'' is part of ''B'' and ''B'' is part of ''C'', then ''A'' is part of ''C'');
* [[Reflexive relation|Reflexive]] – "Everything is part of itself" (''A'' is part of ''A''); and
* [[Antisymmetric relation|Antisymmetric]] – "Nothing is a part of its parts" (If ''A'' is part of ''B'' and ''A'' ≠ ''B'', then ''B'' is not part of ''A'').

Meronomies may be represented in [[semantic web]] languages such as [[Web Ontology Language|OWL]] and [[SKOS]]. In [[natural language]]s they are represented by [[meronymy|meronyms]] and [[holonymy|holonyms]].
